subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
School counsellor note. Dolma, Class 11. Self-referred, first session.
Dolma said she decided about two weeks ago that she wants to end things with Anirban, her boyfriend of five months. She hasn't told him. "He's not a bad person. I just don't feel it any more."
She listed reasons to wait: his birthday is next week; their friends are all in one group and "everyone will take sides"; she's scared he'll cry at school. Meanwhile, she said, he has been planning a surprise for their six-month mark. She twisted her sleeve while saying this and looked close to tears.
We talked about how delaying can feel kind but may add hurt, since Anirban is still hoping and planning. We discussed choosing a private time, face to face, and short, honest words. She wants to tell him after his birthday but before the six-month date. Will check in next week.

qa.q: How long has Dolma been with Anirban?
qa.a: Anirban has been her boyfriend of five months.

qa.q: Why has Dolma delayed telling Anirban?
qa.a: Dolma is afraid of hurting him, of friends taking sides and of him crying at school, so waiting feels kinder.

qa.q: What turning point did the counsellor help Dolma see?
qa.a: That the delay is adding hurt while Anirban plans a surprise; a private, face-to-face talk with short, honest words soon would be kinder.

qa.q: How might Anirban feel if he learns Dolma decided weeks earlier?
qa.a: Anirban might feel foolish and more hurt, realising he was planning a surprise for a relationship that had already ended in Dolma's mind.

grounding: Shows a teen who has privately decided to end a relationship but delays out of fear of hurting him and of friends' reactions, while he keeps hoping.

passage:
Wednesday
It's been nineteen days since I knew. Standing in the canteen queue, Vinita laughing at something, and I just thought: I don't feel it any more. That was it.
And I still haven't said it. Every day there's a reason. Monday was her test. Today she sent me a photo of two movie tickets for Saturday with three hearts. How do you break up with someone holding movie tickets?
And the group. Ruksana has already asked why I'm "being weird". If I end it, everyone will have an opinion by lunch.
So I keep replying "haha yes" and "can't wait". Which is a lie. And every time I send one, she gets a little more excited, and I feel worse.
I think I'm not protecting her. I think I'm protecting me.
Rafiq

qa.q: What did Vinita send a photo of today?
qa.a: Vinita sent a photo of two movie tickets for Saturday with three hearts.

qa.q: What does Rafiq realise by the end of the entry?
qa.a: Rafiq realises the delay isn't protecting Vinita but Rafiq's own comfort, and it is making the guilt worse.

qa.q: What could Rafiq do before Saturday?
qa.a: Rafiq could meet Vinita privately before the film and tell her honestly and briefly, rather than letting her plan more around false hope.

qa.q: How is the delay affecting Vinita?
qa.a: Vinita keeps hoping and getting more excited, planning films and sending hearts, without knowing the relationship is already over for Rafiq.

grounding: Illustrates a teen who has decided a relationship is over but keeps delaying, fearing hurt and gossip, while the other keeps hoping.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Tuesday

I decided today. It's over with Pihu. I don't feel the same. I haven't for weeks.

But I didn't tell her.

She sent me a photo of the keychain she bought for our six-month anniversary next Friday. I said "cute 🙂". I felt sick.

I can't tell her before the anniversary. That would be cruel. And after, there's the class trip, and everyone will know, and Sumit says her friends will make it a whole thing. Her whole group will hate me. So maybe after the trip.

But every day I wait, she plans something else. She's talking about going to the fair together in December.

Sumit said, "The longer you wait, the worse it'll be for her." I know he's right. I just don't want to be the bad guy.

— Vaibhav

qa.q: What did Pihu buy for their six-month anniversary?
qa.a: A keychain.

qa.q: What is Vaibhav afraid of about ending things?
qa.a: Vaibhav fears hurting Pihu and the fuss among friends, especially her group, and doesn't want to be seen as the bad guy.

qa.q: What went wrong with the plan to wait, and what could fix it?
qa.a: Each day of waiting lets Pihu keep hoping and planning; telling her soon, kindly and privately, would cause less pain overall.

qa.q: What is it like for Pihu to plan the fair while Vaibhav has already decided?
qa.a: She is hopeful and excited, unaware it is over, which will make the eventual news harder.

grounding: Vaibhav's diary shows him privately deciding the relationship is over but delaying, afraid of hurting Pihu and of the fuss, while she keeps hoping.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Jyoti had decided it was over with Bittu on the day of the Holi mela, when she watched him argue with the ice-cream man and felt nothing at all.

That was three weeks ago. She still hadn't told him.

Every morning he waited for her at the bus stop at the edge of their village, with a guava or a packet of chana for her. Every morning she took it and said "thank you" and felt worse.

Her cousin Deepika asked at the handpump, "Why are you still with him if you don't like him?"

"Because his sister is my friend. Because the whole village will talk. Because he'll cry."

"He'll cry either way," Deepika said. "Now he's also buying you guavas."

That night Jyoti couldn't sleep. Every guava felt like a small lie she was taking from him.

qa.q: What did Bittu bring for Jyoti at the bus stop?
qa.a: A guava or a packet of chana.

qa.q: How does Jyoti feel every morning when she takes the guava?
qa.a: She feels guilty and worse each time, because she has already decided it is over.

qa.q: What would you advise Jyoti?
qa.a: To tell Bittu soon, kindly and privately, because delaying lets him keep hoping and makes the eventual hurt bigger.

qa.q: What is it like for Bittu to wait at the bus stop each morning?
qa.a: He is hopeful and caring, unaware it is over, and each day he invests a little more.

grounding: Jyoti privately decides it is over with Bittu but delays out of fear of hurting him and of village talk, while he keeps hoping.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Ines had decided on Sunday, walking her dog along the river in Seville: it was over with Jin. She just hadn't told him.
On Monday he saved her a seat in the canteen, as always. On Tuesday he sent a photo of two tickets for the school film night on Friday, with a heart. "Great!" she typed, and disliked herself a little. Her friends would talk; his friends would take sides; and his face, when she said it, would be the worst part. Maybe after the film night. Maybe after exams.
On Thursday, by the lockers, Jin said, "You seem far away. Is it me?"
"No, just tired," she said. She watched his shoulders relax, and felt the lie settle on her, heavier than the truth would have been.

qa.q: What did Jin send Ines on Tuesday?
qa.a: He sent a photo of two tickets for the school film night on Friday, with a heart.

qa.q: Why does Ines keep putting off telling Jin?
qa.a: She is afraid of hurting Jin and dreads the fuss among their friends, so delay feels kinder, though she feels guilty each time she pretends.

qa.q: What turning point does Ines have on Thursday, and what could she do with it?
qa.a: When Jin asks if it is him, she could answer honestly and kindly, in private, instead of saying she's tired and letting him hope longer.

qa.q: How is the delay affecting Jin right now?
qa.a: Jin keeps hoping, saving her seat and buying tickets, and relaxes at her answer, so the ending, when it comes, may hurt him more.

grounding: Shows a teen who has privately decided to end a relationship delaying out of fear of hurting the other, while the other keeps hoping.
